history.period: 16th century (built during the reign of Krishnadevaraya, per local guides; some sources say temple origins trace further back)
history.summary: The Sri Ranganatha Swamy Temple is a Vaishnavite temple inside the historic Penukonda Fort. Penukonda was the Vijayanagara Empire's second capital after the fall of Hampi (capital moved here by Tirumala in 1565, held until 1592), and the temple dates to the Vijayanagara period, credited locally to the reign of Krishnadevaraya. CSV town corrected from Anantapur to Penukonda (temple is inside/at the Penukonda Fort); district corrected from Anantapur to Sri Sathya Sai (2022 bifurcation). Timings (8:00 AM - 1:30 PM, 4:30 PM - 7:30 PM) are from a low-quality blog and should be verified. Coordinates are the Penukonda town/fort anchor (approx. 14.09 N, 77.60 E, corroborated by Wikipedia's fort coordinates), not a verified temple POI.

name: Sri Ranganatha Swamy Temple, Penukonda
town_description: Penukonda is a historic town in Sri Sathya Sai district, about 70-75 km from Anantapur. After the Vijayanagara defeat at Talikota (1565), it became the empire's second capital until 1592. The hill fort (a protected Monument of National Importance) holds palaces, temples, mosques, the Gagan Mahal, the Babaiah Dargah, and is a noted Jain pilgrimage centre.

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru (~150 km); taxi or bus toward Penukonda
travel.railway: Penukonda Railway Station in the town; nearest major junctions Anantapur (~70 km) and Hindupur (~25 km)
travel.road: ~70-75 km from Anantapur on the Anantapur-Hindupur/Bengaluru corridor; APSRTC buses from Anantapur; about 2 hours from Bengaluru by road

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant weather for exploring the fort complex)
visitor_information.opening_hours: 8:00 AM - 1:30 PM and 4:30 PM - 7:30 PM (single low-quality source - verify)
